children: A new venture capital fund, GCVC, launched on Tuesday with backing from a group of corporate general counsels and law firm Wilson Sonsini.
New York-based GCVC said more than 50 general counsels have invested in the fund, which plans to invest in early-stage legal, regulatory and compliance technology startups.
The fund did not immediately respond to a request for comment about how much money the lawyers and Wilson Sonsini have invested.

Erick Rabin, the general counsel and chief compliance officer of loyalty program Bilt Rewards, told Reuters the fund is unique in its approach of being “for lawyers and by lawyers.” He is a general partner alongside Matthew Holbreich, a former Fenwick & West lawyer who is now chief of staff at clinical trial platform Medable, according to his LinkedIn account.
There has been an acceleration of technology startups, including AI companies, that are providing services to lawyers and other professionals, Rabin said.

Investors have been pouring capital into startups marketing new tools for lawyers as AI promises to reshape the legal industry. Among notable deals this year, Sweden-based Legora raised $550 million at ​a $5.55 billion valuation in March, and San Francisco-based Harvey raised $200 million at an $11 billion valuation the same month.

GCVC said it has already invested in Sandstone, an AI legal tech platform for corporate legal departments, and Stilta, an agentic AI platform for patent litigation. The firm did not disclose the size of the investments.

Wilson Sonsini was the first law firm to invest in GCVC, the fund said. A spokesperson for Wilson Sonsini, which is known for its work representing technology companies, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Another venture capital firm dedicated to legal technology investments, The LegalTech Fund, in November 2025 said it closed a second fund at $110 million, backed by investors including law firm McDermott, Will & Schulte.
